04

Graphic language

01Floating windowsAbout · Contact · News and Media

Rounded windows make content feel tactile and creative. Use a light frame, three small header dots, a soft shadow, and a slight tilt or drift to lift important content away from the background.

  • Keep corners generously rounded.
  • Use motion as a gentle accent.
  • Keep text panels quieter than image panels.
✦+
02Angled transitionsHome · About · Media pages

Shallow diagonal bands are an optional way to add energy between major sections. Clean, straight transitions are equally on-brand and often the better choice when the content should feel quieter.

  • Use angles only when extra movement helps.
  • Choose clean edges for simpler layouts.
  • If used, keep text outside the angled edge.
03Glass controlsNavigation · Search · Brainstorm tools

Menus and utility controls sit inside translucent white surfaces. Blur, thin light borders, and dark, substantial icons keep the controls visible over changing backgrounds.

  • Use a 12–14px background blur.
  • Keep primary controls circular.
  • Use Jet Black icons with confident strokes.
04Bubbles & connectorsBrainstorm

The Brainstorm canvas turns the window language into flexible idea bubbles. Soft translucency, colored glow, dotted backgrounds, and dashed links make the space feel playful and useful.

  • Use a soft shadow instead of a heavy outline.
  • Let color identify and group ideas.
  • Keep connectors secondary to the content.
IdeaStory
05Type in the interfaceHeadlines · Navigation · Supporting copy

Arial Black carries names, major headings, labels, and important actions. Myriad Pro supports it with open, conversational paragraphs, captions, and helper text.

  • Use display type to establish hierarchy.
  • Use body type for longer reading.
  • Keep all-caps labels short and well spaced.
Make it
bold.

Then give the details room to breathe.

06Dotted gridHomepage footer · Brainstorm canvas

The dotted grid adds quiet structure and texture without competing with the work. It gives open areas a graphic rhythm while keeping the overall layout clean.

  • Keep the dots small, even, and low contrast.
  • Use the grid in open backgrounds rather than behind dense text.
  • Pair it with bold type, clean panels, or spacious layouts.
Dotted grid
